recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No follow-up is needed in FHIR core unless a future issue intentionally revisits frame-count semantics for Media or Attachment.
issue_request: FHIR-16993 was a Published/Persuasive FHIR-core Media issue requesting removal of Media.frames meaningIfMissing because assuming one frame made it impossible to say the frame count is unknown; the accepted resolution was to remove the meaning and add a note to the comment.
initial_application: The issue was applied in git-svn mirrored commit 7e062875383499b6039d916107ae30c5ae8d9c0b, which removed the Media.frames cell saying systems could assume one frame when absent and added the current unknown-frame-count warning.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini keeps Media in the active build. Later GF#19250 Media-to-DocumentReference work copied the already-correct unknown-frame-count warning to Attachment.frames rather than reintroducing the removed assumption. Jira search found no later Attachment.frames issue changing this conclusion, and community searches found only bot/minutes records plus no conflicting discussion.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. No source edit was needed because source/media/media-spreadsheet.xml already reflects the approved resolution.

related_jiras.note: The Media-to-DocumentReference work is relevant background because it copied the same no-default frame-count warning to Attachment.frames; it was not independently reconciled here.
